title: Boxplot with multi-vari grouping
response: Variable to use for boxplot (a numeric variable)
YaxisGroup: Y variable (a category) variable for Y-axis
XaxisGroup: X variable (a category) variable for X-axis
withinXaxisGroup: One or more grouping (category) variable(s) to group boxplots within x-axis group
showMinMaxNumberChk: Show min and max value per Y-axis category value on the plot
showMeanNumberChk: Show mean value on the plot
showMedianNumberChk: Show median value on the plot
showQuantileNumberChk: Show quantile (Q1 and Q3) value on the plot
showStatTableChk: Print all stats in a table
meanPointColor: Select a color for mean points (After color selection, click outside the control to apply)
keepOriginalScaleChk: Keep the original scale of the numeric variable selected to plot
factorLevelOccuranceOrderChk: Reorder all category variable levels in the order of their occurrence for plotting
legends: Show Legends and if so, position of Legends (default is right)
refPointNote: Note: Specify the lower spec limit (LSL) points, the upper spec limit (USL) points, both, or neither. A set that is left empty is not plotted. For each set, enter one value per Y-axis category value (at least as many values as there are Y-axis category values; any extra values are ignored). Values are matched to the Y-axis category values in the order they first appear in the data (or in sorted order if the reorder-by-occurrence option is not checked). The points are rescaled the same way as the plotted data (within each Y-axis category value) unless the original scale is kept.
lslRefPointValues: Enter comma separated LSL value(s) on the original scale of the numeric variable, e.g. 10, 20, 30
lslRefPointLabels: Specify optional comma separated labels (no enclosing quotes) for the LSL point(s), default label is LSL
lslRefPointColor: Select a color for the LSL points (After color selection, click outside the control to apply)
uslRefPointValues: Enter comma separated USL value(s) on the original scale of the numeric variable, e.g. 40, 50, 60
uslRefPointLabels: Specify optional comma separated labels (no enclosing quotes) for the USL point(s), default label is USL
uslRefPointColor: Select a color for the USL points (After color selection, click outside the control to apply)
lslLabelVjust: LSL label vertical position (vjust): positive = below the point, negative = above (default = 1.8)
lslLabelHjustLow: LSL label horizontal position (hjust) for points in the lower half of the range: negative = text extends right (default = -0.1)
lslLabelHjustHigh: LSL label horizontal position (hjust) for points in the upper half of the range: above 1 = text extends left (default = 1.1)
uslLabelVjust: USL label vertical position (vjust): positive = below the point, negative = above (default = -2.1)
uslLabelHjustLow: USL label horizontal position (hjust) for points in the lower half of the range: negative = text extends right (default = -0.1)
uslLabelHjustHigh: USL label horizontal position (hjust) for points in the upper half of the range: above 1 = text extends left (default = 1.1)
refPointSize: Reference point size, for both LSL and USL points (default = 2.5)

help.title: Boxplot with special grouping (Multi-Vari)
help.body:
Description
Creates horizontal boxplots of a numeric variable, one box for each value of a Y-axis category variable. The category variable can optionally be placed on the X-axis (as separate panels), and optionally the boxes can be grouped further within each X-axis value. This multi-vari style chart is useful for comparing batches, lots, methods, operators or other subgroups.

Variables
Variable to use for boxplot: the numeric variable that is plotted.
Y variable: the category variable that defines the boxes along the Y-axis (required).
X variable: optional category variable that splits the plot into one panel per value.
Grouping variable(s) within X-axis group: optional one or more category variables used to group the boxplots within each X-axis value.

Scale
By default the numeric variable is rescaled to 0-1 separately within each Y-axis category value, so that categories measured on very different scales can be compared on one chart. The X-axis then shows the rescaled values. Check Keep the original scale to plot the original values instead.
Check Reorder all category variable levels in the order of their occurrence to list categories in the order they first appear in the data, instead of sorted order.

Plot options
Flip axis: swaps the X and Y axes.
Connect the mean points / Connect the median points: draws a line through the mean (or median) points across the boxes.
Show mean points: shows the mean points when they are not connected.
Show min and max, mean, median, quantile (Q1 and Q3) values on the plot: prints these numbers on the plot.
Print all stats in a table: prints min, max, mean, median, Q1 and Q3 for each group as a table.

Title, labels and appearance
Chart title, X axis label and Y axis label can be entered. The mean point color and size, the boxplot width (default 0.4), the theme and the legend position (default right) can also be set.

Reference points (specification limits)
Optionally add lower spec limit (LSL) points, upper spec limit (USL) points, both, or neither. Each set is independent: a set whose values field is empty is not plotted.
Values: enter comma separated values on the original scale of the numeric variable, one value for each Y-axis category value, for example 10, 20, 30. Values are matched to the Y-axis category values in the order the categories first appear in the data (or in sorted order if reordering by occurrence is not checked). Unless the original scale is kept, each point is rescaled with the same 0-1 scaling as the plotted data in its category.
Labels (optional): comma separated labels, without quotes, one per point. A point without a label is labelled LSL or USL. The value is always shown in brackets, for example LSL (0.96).
Color: color of the points and their labels for that set (default red for LSL and purple for USL). Point size is shared by both sets (default 2.5).
Label position: each set has a vertical position (vjust; positive puts the label below the point, negative above) and two horizontal positions (hjust). The lower-half hjust is used for points in the lower half of their category's range (default -0.1, text extends to the right) and the upper-half hjust for points in the upper half (default 1.1, text extends to the left), so labels point toward the middle of the panel and are not cut off. Adjust these values if labels overlap other text.
Errors: if a set has fewer values than there are Y-axis category values, or contains a non-numeric value, an error message is printed and that set is not plotted (the other set is still plotted). Extra values beyond the number of categories are ignored, with a note.
